edges.label: Same open-ended French position
edges.reason: Both report Macron leaving future Western deployments open without an agreed plan. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Same original speaker; not independent evidence that a deployment was ordered.

edges.label: Same Macron statement
edges.reason: Both describe the option remaining open despite no consensus. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: The statement is not a commitment by France or all NATO countries to send combat soldiers.

edges.label: Germany’s stated refusal supports one part of the list
edges.reason: China Daily directly quotes Pistorius ruling out German ground troops. That provides a named national statement supporting the Germany component of Sputnik’s wider list.
edges.caveat: Sputnik lists several countries. The supporting passage concerns Germany.
edges.support_scope: The German national position in S02.
edges.direction_reason: CD01 supplies the specified support for S02.
edges.unsupported_parts: The policies of every listed country or a denial of all personnel already in Ukraine.

edges.label: The quoted NATO statement supports the broad account
edges.reason: Censor.NET quotes Stoltenberg specifying no plans for NATO combat troops. That supports the NATO-chief component of Kyiv Independent’s report of responses to Macron.
edges.caveat: The direct quotation is narrower than the general deployment wording in KI03.
edges.support_scope: The NATO combat-deployment-plan component of KI03.
edges.direction_reason: CEN02 supplies the specified support for KI03.
edges.unsupported_parts: Every member state’s policy, all future options or the absence of existing national personnel.

edges.label: Keeping Western troop deployments open versus ruling Germany out
edges.reason: Macron leaves future Western troop deployments open. Pistorius rules out German ground troops. These are contrasting national policy positions in the debate on Western deployments.
edges.caveat: Macron’s Western-wide possibility and Germany’s refusal of its own participation can coexist. They concern different decision-makers and potentially different future conditions. This is a proposed policy contrast, not proof of an inconsistent deployment plan.
edges.direction_reason: Analyst-assigned comparison: KI01 is proposed to contradict CD01. The arrow follows this source-to-target order.

edges.label: Existing special forces versus future combat troops
edges.reason: An anonymous source claims special forces are already there; Stoltenberg says NATO has no combat-deployment plan.
edges.caveat: Different roles, institutions and times; no direct contradiction and no confirmation of the anonymous claim.

edges.label: Two claims with unclear roles
edges.reason: One unnamed official alleges special forces; Zakharova alleges personnel helping operate weapons.
edges.caveat: The people, countries, roles and dates are not matched. Similar allegations are not independent corroboration of the same unit.

edges.label: Possible noncombat role versus alleged presence
edges.reason: France discusses a possible future noncombat role; Zakharova claims personnel already help with weapons.
edges.caveat: Contemplated future deployments and alleged present advisers are different claims.

edges.label: Useful signal versus worrying signal
edges.reason: Väli evaluates the troop discussion as a useful message of support. Tanner calls Macron’s remarks a worrying signal. Their evaluations of the remarks point in different directions.
edges.caveat: This proposed narrative comparison concerns the speakers’ evaluations. A message could be useful in one respect and worrying in another. Review should compare the reasons and scope before deciding on a contradiction.
edges.direction_reason: Analyst-assigned comparison: EP01 is proposed to contradict CD02. The arrow follows this source-to-target order.

edges.label: Same German account of Scholz’s view
edges.reason: Both carry Hebestreit’s description of Scholz’s negative reaction. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Same German government source translated by different outlets, not two independent accounts of every attendee.

edges.label: Message of resolve and signs of division
edges.reason: Väli sees a useful signal; Cui sees disagreement among governments.
edges.caveat: A debate can signal commitment while exposing disagreement, so the assessments need not be incompatible.

edges.label: Talks versus conditional welcome
edges.reason: Zelensky wants new defense ideas and separately welcomes ideas that strengthen Ukraine.
edges.caveat: Neither sentence explicitly approves a NATO combat deployment. They describe related but distinct remarks.

edges.label: What is needed versus claimed lack of results
edges.reason: Väli argues weapons are Ukraine’s priority; Lavrov alleges more weapons have brought no visible results.
edges.caveat: The first is a recommendation about needs; the second is a Russian official’s causal assessment. No matched measurement of the same supplies is given.

edges.label: Same Peskov warning
edges.reason: Both relay Peskov’s prediction of a Russia-NATO confrontation. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Same source, not independent proof that war would follow.

edges.label: Both Russian officials warn of escalation
edges.reason: Peskov predicts direct conflict; Zakharova says Western troops in any form worsen the war. The matching content alone supplies no evidential direction.
edges.caveat: This matches a broad warning, not an identical prediction: the officials specify different outcomes and troop-role scopes.

edges.label: Scholz’s reported objection supports the division account
edges.reason: TASS quotes Germany’s spokesman describing Scholz’s objection to Macron’s proposal. That supplies a specific government disagreement supporting Cui’s interpretation of divisions in the West.
edges.caveat: The arrow uses a reported German reaction to support a specific part of the analyst’s reading.
edges.direction_reason: T02 supplies the specified support for GT02.
edges.unsupported_parts: Every Western government’s view or Cui’s prediction that NATO will avoid direct involvement.

excluded.reason: Pentagon funding and ammunition report; it does not discuss Macron’s remarks or Western troop deployments.

method.country_note: Outlet countries describe origin. Claimant countries describe an office, organization or stated residence, not assumed citizenship.
method.claim_type_note: A fact claim is a checkable statement, not a fact verified by this graph. Opinions, predictions, legal positions and promises are marked separately.
method.edge_note: Green arrows point from a supporting claim to the claim receiving support. Grey comparisons have no assigned direction. Solid red arrows point from a source claim to a target claim it is proposed to contradict. Red direction follows the analyst-assigned comparison order. Every proposed conflict retains its reasoning and scope limits for human review.
method.attention_note: Attention is a qualitative reading of the saved article, with paragraph locators; it is not a measured share of words.
method.endorsement_note: A quoted speaker’s view is separate from the article narrator’s view. No outlet-wide position is inferred from one article.
method.cleaning_note: Uses saved recovered text. Kyiv Independent later Most Popular / News Feed material is excluded; original paragraph numbers retained. FT wrapped lines are joined into logical paragraphs.
